Identity.History: The Painted Stoa (Stoa Poikile) stood on the north side of the Athenian Agora and was famous for the large painted panels that decorated its interior. These works depicted mythological and historical victories, including the Battle of Marathon, turning the building into both a public gathering place and a monument to Athenian identity and military achievement. In later centuries it also became closely associated with the philosopher Zeno, whose followers took the name Stoics from the stoa.
